intro: Requires Solo ambient on mesh1. This lab uses petshop and warehouse. It enables per-pod workload claims near the end; Reset restores the previous ztunnel configuration.

2.1.title: Deploy the petshop application
2.1.say: Create an ambient namespace and deploy an API with four client workloads.
2.1.point: Five pods Running, one container each. ztunnel handles their traffic from the node.

blocks.title: Label the namespace, apply the app

parts.title: Enrol the namespace
parts.instruction: Create petshop with the ambient label.
parts.expect: The namespace is created or configured.

parts.title: Deploy the API and clients
parts.instruction: Apply the petshop resources and wait for all five deployments.
parts.expect: Five pods are Running, with one container each.

blocks.show:
kubectl label namespace petshop istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient
kubectl apply -f demo-scripts/yaml/10-petshop/

2.2.title: Inspect workload certificates
2.2.say: A workload's identity is its mTLS certificate, issued for its ServiceAccount. That is what policy matches on.
2.2.point: The two checkout deployments use the same ServiceAccount. Their SPIFFE identity is mesh1/ns/petshop/sa/checkout.

blocks.title: Pods next to the certs ztunnel holds

parts.title: List the ServiceAccounts
parts.instruction: List each pod beside the ServiceAccount it runs as.
parts.expect: checkout-blue and checkout-green both use checkout.

parts.title: Read the certificates
parts.instruction: Read the leaf certificates held by the ztunnel on the application node.
parts.expect: There is a checkout ServiceAccount certificate, rather than a separate identity for each checkout pod.

blocks.show:
kubectl -n petshop get pods \
  -o custom-columns=POD:...,SERVICEACCOUNT:...
istioctl ztunnel-config certificates <ztunnel>

checks.label: Both checkout pods run as sa/checkout

2.3.title: Allow storefront to call petstore
2.3.say: Apply an L4 policy that permits the storefront ServiceAccount, then check all four callers.
2.3.point: Once an ALLOW selects petstore, anything it does not name is denied. ztunnel fails closed.

blocks.title: Allow storefront, then call from all four

parts.title: Apply the ALLOW policy
parts.instruction: Select petstore and allow mesh1/ns/petshop/sa/storefront on port 8080.
parts.expect: allow-storefront is applied. Callers not covered by an ALLOW policy are denied.

parts.title: Compare client results
parts.instruction: Read the latest request result from each client.
parts.expect: storefront returns 200. analytics and both checkout clients cannot connect.

blocks.show:
kind: AuthorizationPolicy   # action: ALLOW
  selector: app=petstore
  principals:
  - mesh1/ns/petshop/sa/storefront

2.4.title: Read the connection decisions
2.4.say: Every allow and deny is logged by ztunnel, with the caller's SPIFFE identity on the line.
2.4.point: The inbound DENY lines read "allow policies exist, but none allowed". That is the fail-closed rule from 2.3.

blocks.title: ztunnel's access log for petshop
blocks.instruction: Read recent petshop connections from ztunnel's access log.
blocks.expect: Allowed and denied connections include the source identity. Denials identify the policy decision.

checks.label: A denied caller, with its identity
Reason: fail closed
checks.match: allow policies exist, but none allowed

2.5.title: Allow a shared ServiceAccount
2.5.say: Allow the checkout identity and compare the two pods that use it.
2.5.point: An identity-only rule allows both checkout pods because they share a ServiceAccount. Per-pod claims let the policy distinguish them later.

blocks.title: Allow sa/checkout, call from both pods

parts.title: Allow the checkout identity
parts.instruction: Add a second ALLOW policy for the checkout ServiceAccount.

parts.title: Compare the checkout pods
parts.instruction: Read the clients' latest results after the policy update.
parts.expect: Both checkout pods return 200; analytics remains denied.

2.6.title: Test namespace policies and explicit DENY
2.6.say: Add a caller in warehouse. Allow its namespace, remove that access, then test an explicit DENY.
2.6.point: Two denials look the same from the client. ztunnel's log tells them apart: "none allowed" versus "explicitly denied by".

blocks.title: A caller in another namespace

parts.title: Deploy the warehouse client
parts.instruction: Create an ambient warehouse namespace and a client that calls petstore.

parts.title: Check the initial denial
parts.instruction: Read the warehouse pod's status and latest request.
parts.expect: The pod is Running but its call is denied. No policy allows warehouse yet.

blocks.show:
# namespace warehouse, sa/warehouse-svc
kubectl apply -f warehouse.yaml

parts.title: Allow both namespaces
parts.instruction: Apply an ALLOW policy for callers from petshop or warehouse.

parts.title: Check warehouse access
parts.instruction: Read a request from storefront and warehouse-svc.

parts.title: Remove warehouse from the allowed set
parts.instruction: Update the namespace policy to permit petshop only.
parts.expect: The policy is configured without warehouse.

parts.title: Read the denied connection
parts.instruction: Read the warehouse result and the corresponding ztunnel denial.
parts.expect: The client cannot connect. ztunnel reports that no ALLOW policy matched.

checks.label: ztunnel: none allowed
checks.match: allow policies exist, but none allowed

blocks.title: Explicit DENY on analytics

parts.title: Deny analytics explicitly
parts.instruction: Apply a DENY policy for the analytics ServiceAccount, which the namespace policy otherwise permits.

parts.title: Check which policy denied the call
parts.instruction: Compare storefront and analytics, then read the denial reason.
parts.expect: storefront returns 200. analytics is denied by l4-deny-analytics.

blocks.show:
kind: AuthorizationPolicy   # action: DENY
  principals:
  - mesh1/ns/petshop/sa/analytics

blocks.title: Remove the namespace policies
blocks.instruction: Delete the two policies introduced in this chapter.
blocks.show:
kubectl -n petshop delete authorizationpolicy \
  l4-allow-petshop-namespace l4-deny-analytics

2.7.title: Authorise using per-pod claims
2.7.say: Enable workload claims, assign a tier to each checkout deployment and allow only the gold tier.
2.7.point: checkout-blue returns 200 and checkout-green is denied. The policy distinguishes them using a signed claim in their certificates.

blocks.title: Turn on workload claims
blocks.instruction: Enable workload claims in ztunnel and wait for its rollout.
blocks.expect: The daemon set is ready and ENABLE_WORKLOAD_CLAIMS is true.

blocks.title: Inspect per-pod certificates
blocks.instruction: Read ztunnel's checkout certificates after enabling workload claims.
blocks.expect: Each checkout pod has its own leaf certificate, with the same ServiceAccount identity.

blocks.title: Tag the pods gold and silver
blocks.instruction: Annotate checkout-blue as gold and checkout-green as silver. Wait for the updated pods.
blocks.expect: The pod annotations show gold for blue and silver for green.
blocks.show:
# annotation solo.io.security-claims/tier
kubectl patch deploy checkout-blue  ... gold
kubectl patch deploy checkout-green ... silver

blocks.title: Read the signed tier claims
blocks.instruction: Decode the leaf certificates issued to the two checkout pods.
blocks.expect: Both contain the checkout SPIFFE URI. Their signed tier claims differ.
blocks.show:
istioctl ztunnel-config certificates <ztunnel> \
  -o json | openssl x509 -text

parts.title: Apply the claims policy
parts.instruction: Remove the broad checkout ALLOW and permit the checkout identity only when its signed tier is gold.

parts.title: Test both checkout pods
parts.instruction: Allow time for the policy to propagate, then make a fresh request from each pod.
